name: Ceuta
title: Ceuta Ship Thickness Gauging | UTM for Bunkering Hub Ships
description: Ship thickness gauging in Ceuta, the Strait of Gibraltar bunkering port: hull, tank and piping UTM for tankers, bulkers, ferries and passing ships.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement in Ceuta on the Strait of Gibraltar
intro: Ceuta is a Spanish port on the African shore of the Strait of Gibraltar. It is best known as a bunkering stop for ships that never intended to enter the Mediterranean ports further on, and as the other end of the ferry run from Algeciras. Stays are short and tied to fuel deliveries. Atlantis NDT mobilises an ultrasonic gauging team from India to the ship and shapes the readings around the time available alongside or at anchor.

highlights.h: Gauging fitted to a bunkering stop
highlights.p: A ship loading fuel at Ceuta has a defined number of hours alongside or at anchor. We choose the spaces that matter most, such as suspect ballast tanks or piping, so that the readings finish before the hoses come off.
Ceuta lies a short sea crossing from Algeciras and the Bay of Gibraltar. A team travelling for one ship can often continue to a second ship or a nearby drydock without a separate trip from India.

highlights.h: Passing tonnage with questions about steel
highlights.p: Bulk carriers, tankers and container ships on the Europe–Asia and Atlantic routes divert here for fuel. Owners use the stop to sample ballast tanks and decks before a charter, a sale or a docking.

port.h: Ceuta: a Spanish enclave port with bunkering, ferries and fishing
p: Ceuta is a Spanish autonomous city on the southern side of the Strait of Gibraltar, bordering Morocco, and its port is run by the Autoridad Portuaria de Ceuta. The harbour sits at the foot of Monte Hacho on the eastern side of the isthmus, with commercial and passenger quays in the main basin and a separate fishing harbour. Vehicle and passenger ferries cross to Algeciras throughout the day, carrying commuters, holiday traffic and freight, and the crossing is the lifeline of the city.

Bunkering is the commercial engine. Ships passing through the Strait can stop at Ceuta, take fuel from barges or from the quay, and carry on without the delays of a larger port. Bulk carriers, tankers, container ships and car carriers all appear in the roadstead, usually for a few hours, sometimes longer when waiting for weather or instructions. Small cargo ships bring supplies for the city, and fishing boats work from their own basin. A cruise call is occasional rather than regular.

The geography brings challenges. The Strait funnels wind, and the easterly known as the Levante can build quickly and stop launch operations at the anchorage, while the opposing Poniente can bring a swell into the western side of the port. Strong currents flow through the Strait, and ships at anchor can swing in ways that make boarding uncomfortable. A Ceuta gauging job therefore carries weather risk in the plan, and for anything larger than a few spaces it makes sense to use Ceuta to collect data and finish the programme at a yard, where the ship is on the blocks and the technicians have full access.

facilities.h: Quays, anchorage and fishing basin: where gauging can be done in Ceuta
p: At the commercial quays, ships working cargo or waiting to bunker can be gauged in spaces that do not interfere with operations. Ballast tanks released by the chief officer, deck plating, hatch coamings, deck piping and the steering gear flat are the usual targets, and a tanker taking bunkers can have its deck structure and accessible tanks measured once the permit system is in place. Ferries on the Algeciras run are measured between crossings or during off-season stops, with attention on the vehicle deck, ramp and stern door.

At the anchorage, the plan depends on weather and on how long the ship stays. A launch arranged through the agent brings the technicians to the ship, and their ultrasonic gauges and magnetic particle kit travel in cases that go up the pilot ladder or accommodation ladder with them. Ceuta has facilities for light repairs and for small craft, but a full docking of a large merchant ship normally means a yard on the Spanish mainland or in the Bay of Gibraltar. The readings taken at Ceuta then go to that yard as a starting point, and the team can follow the ship there to finish the survey if the owner wants a single contractor for the whole job.
list: Main commercial quays: ballast tank, deck and piping gauging on ships working cargo or waiting for bunkers
Bunker berths and roadstead: targeted readings on tankers, bulkers and container ships taking fuel, by launch where the ship is at anchor
Ferry berths: vehicle deck, ramp, stern door and ballast gauging on the Algeciras ro-pax ships between crossings
Fishing basin: hull, tank and deck gauging on fishing boats hauled or moored for maintenance
Drydocks in the Bay of Gibraltar and on the mainland: where gauging begun in Ceuta can be finished during the docking survey

context.h: Spanish regulation at the Strait and what drives gauging here
p: Although Ceuta lies on the African coast, it is Spanish territory and part of the EU, and port state control on foreign ships is carried out under the Paris MoU by Spanish marine inspectors, working for the Dirección General de la Marina Mercante through the local Capitanía Marítima. The port lies east of the western boundary of the Mediterranean emission control area, so ships bunkering here operate under the 0.10% sulphur limit or run exhaust gas cleaning systems, and scrubber piping is a recurring subject of gauging on the ships that pass through.

The commercial context is the Strait itself. Ships in transit take fuel at Ceuta because it is convenient and competitive against other Strait ports, and superintendents use the short stay to settle small questions about steel. Typical drivers are a port state control remark, a charterer's request for a condition report, an upcoming sale or a surveyor's note at the last annual survey. The EU Emissions Trading System has covered shipping since 2024 and FuelEU Maritime since 2025, so older ships are under pressure, and a current gauging record shows a buyer or an owner what steel work remains. Owners should also remember that ships calling at EU ports are expected to hold an Inventory of Hazardous Materials, which is separate from thickness gauging but part of the same compliance picture.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Ceuta
jobs.p: Ceuta jobs are short, specific and tied to a fuel delivery or a ferry timetable. We ask for the expected time alongside or at anchor, the spaces the ship can make safe and the report format wanted, then choose a scope that fits. Larger programmes are planned for a nearby yard. Typical requests include:
list: Ballast tank and deck gauging on a bulk carrier at anchor during bunkering, ahead of a special survey at a yard later in the year.
Pre-purchase condition gauging on a product tanker, sampling deck plating, accessible ballast tanks and deck piping during a bunker stop.
Vehicle deck, ramp and stern door readings on a Strait ro-pax ferry during an off-season lay-over.
Fire main, ballast and sea-water piping gauging on a container ship after a port state control remark on corroded pipework.
Hull and tank gauging on a fishing boat out of the water for maintenance in the fishing basin.

logistics: Ceuta has no scheduled commercial airline service of significance, so technicians normally fly from India to Málaga, Jerez or Seville through a European or Gulf hub, then reach Algeciras by road and cross by ferry. The crossing is short but is subject to weather. Spain is in the Schengen area and Schengen visas are needed before travel dates are set. The ship's agent arranges port access, ISPS passes and any launch for the anchorage.
vessels: Ro-pax ferries on the Algeciras route

faqs.q: Is a bunker stop at Ceuta long enough to gauge a ship?
faqs.a: For targeted work, usually. A few hours is enough for a suspect ballast tank, a deck area or a run of piping. A full renewal survey does not fit. Send us the expected stay and the list of spaces, and we will say plainly what is realistic.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a ship at the Ceuta anchorage?
faqs.a: Yes, when weather allows. Boarding is by launch through the agent, and a strong Levante can stop it. Our plan always includes a margin for weather, and where the ship will soon berth or dock we may suggest moving the work alongside.

faqs.q: Where would a ship dock if the Ceuta readings show serious wastage?
faqs.a: That is the owner's and class's decision. Nearby options are yards in the Bay of Gibraltar and on the Spanish mainland. We give the chosen yard the Ceuta readings as an early steel estimate, and the technicians can continue to the yard for the full survey.

faqs.q: Does the Mediterranean emission control area apply at Ceuta?
faqs.a: Yes. The port lies inside the area, so ships here run on compliant fuel or use a scrubber. Where a scrubber is fitted, we recommend gauging the wash-water and overboard piping, because acidic wash water and shell connections wear steel faster than most owners expect.
